title: Increasing Access - LinkedIn
snippet:
**Not sure where to start?** The **Advertising API**, **Community Management API**, **Events Management API**, **Lead Sync API**, **Conversions API**, and **Matched Audiences API** are open to all approved developers — apply through the standard process. Access to **Audience Insights** and **Media Planning** APIs is restricted to developers who meet additional qualification criteria evaluated by LinkedIn. The **Company Intelligence API** is not currently accepting new applications.

The Advertising API and Community Management API each have two access tiers with different access criteria. All applications start with Development tier. You must apply separately to upgrade to the Standard tier.
- Advertising API: Development tier is designed to build end-to-end workflows and supports read-only access for unlimited ad accounts and edit capabilities for up to five (5) Ad Accounts. Standard tier is designed to support campaign management solutions including edit capabilities for unlimited ad accounts.
- Community Management API: Development tier is designed to build and test integrations with API call restrictions. You must complete your integration and testing within twelve months of receiving the API access. Standard tier is designed for live production with no restrictions.

title: Advertising - Overview - LinkedIn
snippet:
The Advertising API enables developers to manage LinkedIn's campaign management platform on behalf of clients through APIs. These APIs provide all features available in LinkedIn Campaign Manager, including creation and management of ad accounts, campaign groups, campaigns, creatives, ad types, and analytics.
With access to the Advertising API program, developers can create and manage Ad Accounts entirely through APIs without depending on the LinkedIn Campaign Manager UI. API calls succeed only when made with correct scopes/permissions assigned to the app after the vetting process. Once the developer application has the required permissions, all Advertising Account features can be accessed by passing identifiers from API responses in the hierarchy.
## Core Components
### Ad Accounts
LinkedIn enables you to create Ad Accounts for your organization's advertising campaigns. Each Ad Account supports:
- Maximum 5,000 campaigns
- Maximum 15,000 creatives
- Requires Enterprise or Business Ad Account with one authenticated user as account administrator
### Account Users
The [Ad Account Users](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/marketing/integrations/ads/account-structure/create-and-manage-account-users?view=li-lms-2026-08) enables advertisers to manage ad account user access. Ad account users are members who have ad account permissions in LinkedIn Campaign Manager. Partners can control user roles for granular access management.

| API Product | Availability | How to Request |
|---|---|---|
| Advertising API | Vetted Product with development and standard tiers | Use the increasing access link to [apply](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/marketing/quick-start?view=li-lms-2026-08#step-2-get-started-with-the-advertising-api). |

title: LinkedIn Marketing API Program Access Tiers - LinkedIn
snippet:
LinkedIn has two tiers of access to our Advertising API: Development and Standard.
The tier assigned to your app defines how many [Ad Accounts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/marketing/integrations/ads/account-structure/create-and-manage-accounts?view=li-lms-2026-09) you can manage through the APIs. Upgrade to the next access tier by meeting the requirements described for that next level. Please note that all API Calls at all access levels are made on production data. Also, use of LinkedIn's Campaign Management APIs is subject to our [LinkedIn Marketing API Program Terms](https://business.linkedin.com/marketing-solutions/marketing-partners/become-a-partner/marketing-developer-program/terms-and-conditions).

| Tier | Description |
|---|---|
| Development | Build end-to-end workflows. |
| Standard | Support campaign management for multiple accounts. |

title: LinkedIn API Partner Support - LinkedIn
snippet:
To access LinkedIn APIs, log in to the [LinkedIn Developer Portal](https://developer.linkedin.com/) with your LinkedIn credentials and create an application.
Within the LinkedIn Developer Portal:
1. Navigate to the **My Apps** section.
2. Click **Create App** and configure your application details.
3. Once the app is created, go to the **Products** tab and select the API products you want to request access to.
Different business lines have different requirements and eligibility criteria. Some allow immediate access without approval; others require a vetting process and use-case review before access can be granted.
For example, [LinkedIn Marketing APIs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/marketing/quick-start#step-1-apply-for-api-access) use a tiered vetting process. Development tier access lets you build and test your integration with limited capabilities. Once your integration meets the business line requirements, you can request standard tier access for full production functionality and broader API usage.
Access to LinkedIn APIs is granted based on the intended use case and compliance with LinkedIn business line requirements. LinkedIn reserves the right to review applications and approve API access at its discretion.

The tier upgrade from Development to Standard is only needed to create Ads for more than 5 Ad Accounts using the POST method.
To request a tier upgrade:
1. Log in to the [LinkedIn Developer Portal](https://developer.linkedin.com/).
2. Navigate to **My Apps → Select the app → Products**.
3. Locate the **Advertising API** product.
4. Review your current access tier.

title: LinkedIn API Pricing: Complete Guide for 2026
snippet:
Two pieces of the **LinkedIn API**, LinkedIn’s set of OAuth 2.0 developer products, are open permissions any developer can switch on without approval: Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect, and Share on LinkedIn, which lets a member post, comment and like as themselves through `w_member_social`. A few others, like the Verified on LinkedIn Development tier, are self-serve on request. The ones most products need, posting to Company Pages through the Community Management API and running ads through the Advertising API (the Marketing Developer Platform, or MDP, in LinkedIn’s own token docs and in most guides), wait on LinkedIn’s approval, and LinkedIn lists no dollar price for any of its API products.

LinkedIn’s own [API Terms of Use](https://www.linkedin.com/legal/l/api-terms-of-use) put it in one line: “The APIs are currently provided for free, but LinkedIn reserves the right to charge for the APIs in the future.” The $699/month figure you’ll see quoted around the web is a third-party estimate, not a LinkedIn price. The table below shows both: what LinkedIn publishes, and what the estimates say.

| Access tier | Official cost (LinkedIn) | Third-party estimate | Best for | Key friction |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Consumer (Sign In with LinkedIn) | Free | $0 (no estimate needed) | Auth flows, basic profile, share to own feed | Tiny scopes, no analytics, no pages |
| Marketing Developer Platform | Not publicly priced. Partner-gated. | $699+/month, per [Phyllo](https://www.getphyllo.com/post/how-much-does-the-linkedin-api-cost-iv). Labeled an estimate by Phyllo itself, with no methodology published. | Pages, ads, scheduling on behalf of clients | Partner approval required, no published timeline (builders report weeks to months) |
| Community Management API | Not publicly priced. Partner-gated. | No separate estimate. Same Developer Portal vetting flow as the other Marketing APIs, with its own access form and screencast review. | Posting, commenting, moderation on company pages | Its own Community Management API approval, Development tier first, then Standard |
| Sales Navigator API | SNAP partner program is closed to new applicants per LinkedIn’s official Sales API docs. Customer-side Sales Nav seats start at $119.99/mo Core or $159.99/mo Advanced. | No credible API estimate. The seat prices are the only real numbers. | Sales tools, lead intelligence, account data | LinkedIn is not currently accepting new SNAP partners. |

title: Integration Requirements for Advertising API - LinkedIn
snippet:
LinkedIn is in the process of rolling out a Technical Sign Off process for the Advertising API program. This ensures that our members get the best experience whether using LinkedIn's native UI or a partner product. The technical review and sign off also ensures that there are no gaps in integrations and that partner products keep up with the latest features and updates released by LinkedIn.
As an API partner, please go through the requirements listed below. These are the capabilities that an integrating partner is expected to build in their product. We request you to plan and incorporate these features early in your design. When you're nearing completion, you must initiate a Technical Sign Off request by contacting your LinkedIn POC on the Business Development team.

| | **Basics** |
| ADS-001 | Demonstrate OAuth 2.0 integration, with right scopes, consent screen. |
| ADS-002 | Demonstrate ability to periodically verify that an access token is valid (heartbeat /me). |
| ADS-003 | Demonstrate ability to detect access token expiry. |
| ADS-004 | Demonstrate ability to re-trigger OAuth Flow in case token has expired or been invalidated. |
| ADS-005 | Demonstrate ability to use refresh tokens to mint new access tokens. |
| ADS-006 | Demonstrate ability to detect refresh token expiry and re-trigger OAuth Flow. |
| | **Account Structure (Hierarchy) and Basic control** |
| ADS-101 | Demonstrate ability to retrieve all Sponsored Accounts with status for the logged in user. |
| ADS-102 | Demonstrate ability to retrieve all CampaignsGroups with status within Sponsored Accounts. |
| ADS-103 | Demonstrate ability to retrieve all Campaigns with status within Sponsored Accounts. |
| ADS-104 | Demonstrate ability to retrieve all Creatives with status within Campaigns. |
| ADS-105 | Demonstrate ability to visualize account hierarchy (accounts -> Creative (Ad)). |
| ADS-106 | Demonstrate ability to PAUSE and ACTIVATE existing Campaigns and Creatives. |
